[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]BACKGROUND[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Across the border, the United States had spent thirty years rebuilding under military governments. Its heir, the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832726][color=#7FDBFF]New American Union[/color][/url][color=white], still considered the West a lost province. In 2049, with Los Vales still wounded by the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832551][color=#7FDBFF]Droid War[/color][/url][color=white] and its networks rebuilt only three years earlier, the Union decided the time had come to reunite the continent.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE WAR[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]It was the most destructive war in the country’s history. Valian cities were bombed, [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Valewood[/color][/url][color=white] burned, [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999863][color=#7FDBFF]Route 69[/color][/url][color=white] became a line of craters, and the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2830623][color=#7FDBFF]Illuminated Favela[/color][/url][color=white] was razed while the walls of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Zyxtopia[/color][/url][color=white] held. As a country, Los Vales was practically destroyed.[/color]

[color=white]The corporations were not. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]WM[/color][/url][color=white], rebuilt as a defense contractor, [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]ArmaTech[/color][/url][color=white], which sold weapons to whoever paid, and [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Automa[/color][/url][color=white]’s robot armies held the invasion. President [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2557482][color=#7FDBFF]Rafael Duarte[/color][/url][color=white] refused to leave Zyxtopia during the siege and coordinated the defense from inside its walls. He is the only president of the Free States remembered with some affection.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE CAMPAIGN[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]At dawn on 6 March, in [/color][color=white][b]Operation Long Road[/b][/color][color=white], three Union columns of about 400,000 soldiers each crossed the border. The northern column marched on [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832735][color=#7FDBFF]Universalia[/color][/url][color=white] and Route 69, the central one on Zyxtopia, the southern one on Valewood. Route 69 was cut in the first week, and 96,000 civilians died in the border towns.[/color]

[color=white]In April the Union bombers reached Valewood. [/color][color=white][b]Operation Burning Reel[/b][/color][color=white] lasted nine nights: the studios, the film archives and the hills burned, and 214,000 people died with the city’s history.[/color]

[color=white]In May the central column surrounded Zyxtopia, three years old as a capital and eleven years in the building. President Duarte refused to leave. During [/color][color=white][b]the Siege of Zyxtopia[/b][/color][color=white] 71,000 Union soldiers died at the walls, and the walls held. Outside them there was nothing to hold: in June, in [/color][color=white][b]Operation Favela Line[/b][/color][color=white], the Union razed the Illuminated Favela to deny its soldiers cover. With 540,000 civilian dead, it was the deadliest operation of the war.[/color]

[color=white]In August Automa released the [/color][color=white][b]Locust[/b][/color][color=white], and in one week 188,000 Union soldiers were killed. The columns broke.[/color]

[color=white]In September and October WM pushed the Union back along Route 69, town by town. [/color][color=white][b]Iron Tide[/b][/color][color=white] was the costliest operation for WM, with 151,000 dead, and for the towns of the road, with 381,000: the retreating Union burned everything it left behind. On 30 November, in [/color][color=white][b]Operation Cease Fire[/b][/color][color=white], the last Union units crossed back over the border. No treaty was ever signed.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE LOCUST[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The war was decided in one week of August. Automa had never shown the [/color][color=white][b]Locust[/b][/color][color=white] to anyone: two million small drones that needed no pilot, talked to each other and chose their own targets. Released over the desert, they found the Union columns faster than any radar and did not stop until there was nothing left to find. It was the first autonomous swarm ever used in a war. Every army in the world has one now. Los Vales sells them.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]DESTRUCTION[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The Bubblepedia counts about 1.6 million Valian dead, 1.3 million of them civilians, and about 420,000 Union soldiers. The country lost more people in nine months than in every other war of its history together.[/color]

[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]CONSEQUENCES[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The Union withdrew without what it came for. When the smoke cleared, the ruins, the money and the reconstruction all belonged to the corporations. In 2050 Duarte and the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999866][color=#7FDBFF]Cabinet[/color][/url][color=white] launched the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2834884][color=#7FDBFF]Rebirth Plan[/color][/url][color=white] — total economic freedom, rebuilt cities, open borders — and millions came. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Zyx[/color][/url][color=white] paid for most of it. Nobody asked what it wanted in return.[/color]

[color=white]The Union has never signed a peace. In 2088 it still wants the West back, and the general who leads it, [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832726][color=#7FDBFF]Marcus Holt[/color][/url][color=white], is the son of the general who lost.[/color]

[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]CAUSES[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The environmental crisis was not only Valian. Around the world, water and food became the most disputed resources on the planet — and since [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]WM[/color][/url][color=white]’s nuclear secrets began leaking in 2022, every power had the bomb. In 2067 the fight over the rivers and fields of Central Asia pulled the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832727][color=#7FDBFF]Neo-Soviet bloc[/color][/url][color=white], armed by [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832714][color=#7FDBFF]RedStar Combine[/color][/url][color=white], into open war with the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832728][color=#7FDBFF]Pacific Union[/color][/url][color=white] led by Japan and [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832714][color=#7FDBFF]Nakama[/color][/url][color=white], with [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832714][color=#7FDBFF]Drexler[/color][/url][color=white]’s Europe dragged in between.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE FRONTS[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The war had three fronts. In [/color][color=white][b]Central Asia[/b][/color][color=white], where it began, armies fought for rivers and wheat fields that were drying up under them. In the [/color][color=white][b]North Pacific[/b][/color][color=white], the navies of Japan and the Neo-Soviet bloc fought for the sea lanes and the islands between them. And from 2069 the war reached [/color][color=white][b]Europe[/b][/color][color=white], when the Neo-Soviet armies crossed into the eastern provinces of the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832708][color=#7FDBFF]European Federation[/color][/url][color=white] to take its farmland.[/color]

[color=white]China and India stayed out and sold rare earths to both sides — until [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]BeDay Astral[/color][/url][color=white] began bringing the same metals down from space at half the price. Africa and South America stayed out and sold food. Los Vales stayed out and sold everything.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE CAMPAIGN[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]In March 2067, in [/color][color=white][b]Operation Dry River[/b][/color][color=white], the Neo-Soviet armies crossed into the river valleys of Central Asia and took the dams. In 2068 the war moved to the sea: [/color][color=white][b]Kuril Fire[/b][/color][color=white], a year of naval battles in the North Pacific, ended with half of both fleets on the bottom and neither side in control.[/color]

[color=white]In the winter of 2069, in [/color][color=white][b]Iron Winter[/b][/color][color=white], the Neo-Soviet bloc invaded the eastern provinces of the European Federation. It was the bloodiest campaign of the war: 4.2 million civilians died in the cold and the fighting, and Europe entered the war on the Pacific side.[/color]

[color=white]In 2070 both sides used the bomb. In the [/color][color=white][b]Aral Exchange[/b][/color][color=white] four tactical warheads fell over the Aral basin in three days — the first nuclear weapons used since [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832719][color=#7FDBFF]Hermosa[/color][/url][color=white]. The basin has been empty ever since. Nobody used the bomb again, but nobody needed to: in 2071 the blockades and the dead fields brought the [/color][color=white][b]Long Hunger[/b][/color][color=white], a famine that killed 22 million people without a single shot. The food that might have saved them was for sale in Los Vales, at the price of gold.[/color]

[color=white]In 2072 the Pacific Union and Europe launched the [/color][color=white][b]Last Offensive[/b][/color][color=white] into the mountains of Central Asia. It stalled in the passes. In June 2073 the exhausted powers signed the [/color][color=white][b]Armistice of Almaty[/b][/color][color=white]: the borders went back to where they had been in 2066, and no one won.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE REST FRONT[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The war’s one new technology did not kill anyone. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Zyx[/color][/url][color=white] sold armies the [/color][color=white][b]Rest Front[/b][/color][color=white]: instead of sending soldiers home on leave, commanders sent them into a [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832550][color=#7FDBFF]Psychoverse[/color][/url][color=white] for a week — a beach, a family, a peace that did not exist — and back to the trenches. It kept millions of soldiers fighting for six years. It also sent home, in 2073, millions of veterans who could no longer sleep without a dose. The same year Los Vales made the basic Psychoverse of every city free. Zyx already knew who its first customers would be.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]LOS VALES AT WAR[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Los Vales declared neutrality and profited like no one else. When the war closed the mines on Earth, the rare metals every army needed came from space — from the asteroid mines of BeDay Astral. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]ArmaTech[/color][/url][color=white] sold weapons to every side, [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Automa[/color][/url][color=white] rented out robot armies, the port of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Ferox[/color][/url][color=white] never stopped, the agricorps sold food for its weight in gold, and Zyx found two new markets: [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832746][color=#7FDBFF]Velocitas[/color][/url][color=white] for soldiers who needed to fight faster, and the Rest Front for those who needed to survive months of combat without losing their minds.[/color]

[color=white]About 64,000 Valian contractors — WM soldiers, Automa technicians, ArmaTech instructors — died abroad. None of them were counted as Valian war dead, because Los Vales was not at war.[/color]

[color=white]Nakama demanded that [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Kizuna[/color][/url][color=white] come home and build Japan’s war networks. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832541][color=#7FDBFF]Aiko Mori[/color][/url][color=white] refused; Japan named Kizuna an enemy, and Los Vales named it a symbol.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]CONSEQUENCES[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The war ended with no clear winner and exhausted powers. The Neo-Soviet bloc lost almost a generation. The European Federation came out poorer and older. Japan never forgave Kizuna. China and India lost their monopoly on rare earths to BeDay Astral, and the race for space that followed became the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832697][color=#7FDBFF]Orbital Conflict[/color][/url][color=white] of 2076.[/color]

[color=white]In Africa, where the famine had been watched from close by, the Concord answered with the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832686][color=#7FDBFF]Treaty of Lagos[/color][/url][color=white] (2075): no foreign company may buy its land or its water. Los Vales came out as the richest country in the world, and that same year used the money to launch [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832550][color=#7FDBFF]Total Connection[/color][/url][color=white]: free dreams for everyone.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE STRAIT CRISIS (2036)[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]In 2036 China closed the export of rare earths. Chips tripled in price, [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832720][color=#7FDBFF]Kizuna Lens[/color][/url][color=white] disappeared from the shops and [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Kizuna[/color][/url][color=white] nearly went bankrupt. In Los Vales, one company drew the lesson: if the metals of the Earth could be closed, the metals of the sky could not. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]BeDay[/color][/url][color=white] began to plan its move into space.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE CHIP EMBARGO (2071)[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]When BeDay Astral began bringing asteroid metal down by the ton, China accused it of "colonizing space" and cut off [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832714][color=#7FDBFF]Tianlong[/color][/url][color=white] chips for six months. Kizuna Lens were again impossible to find, and their price tripled. Half the chips inside them are still Tianlong’s.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE ORBITAL CONFLICT (2076–2078)[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]In orbit the war was never declared. Satellites went dark, asteroids changed owners in the middle of the night, and in 2077 a BeDay Astral station exploded with [/color][color=white][b]41 people[/b][/color][color=white] aboard. Nobody claimed it. BeDay blames Tianlong; Tianlong blames Vayu; Vayu blames the debris.[/color]

[color=white]Nobody won the Orbital Conflict either. BeDay Astral came out of it with the most asteroids, and the treaty of 2078 that ended it does not mention the station at all.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]JAPAN AGAINST KIZUNA[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Since 2018 Japan and Kizuna have fought a cold war of patents and spies: Nakama sues, Kizuna counter-sues, engineers disappear in both directions. In [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832555][color=#7FDBFF]World War III[/color][/url][color=white] Japan demanded that Kizuna come home; [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832541][color=#7FDBFF]Aiko Mori[/color][/url][color=white] refused, and Japan named Kizuna an enemy.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE STRAIT WAR[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]In 2036 China closed its exports of rare earths and the Pacific Union answered with a naval blockade of the Strait. The [/color][color=white][b]Strait War[/b][/color][color=white] (2036–2037) was short and fought mostly at sea and on the networks. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Zyx[/color][/url][color=white]’s hackers — the old [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]ArmaTech[/color][/url][color=white] team — were rented to both sides, and Los Vales discovered the doctrine it still follows: [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832738][color=#7FDBFF][b]neutral, but for sale[/b][/color][/url][color=white].[/color]

[color=white]The war lasted fourteen months and changed no border. It ended with a paper peace that reopened the rare-earth trade, and with one lesson for Los Vales: a company that sells to both sides of a war cannot lose it.[/color]

[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]HOW A TOWN DIES[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Through the 2030s and 2040s the megacorps invested only in the cities they controlled: jobs, technology, hospitals, schools and private security were there and nowhere else. In small and medium towns the administrations were dismantled, local businesses were bought and closed, natural resources were fenced off, and advertising painted life outside the metropolises as backwardness. The towns died one by one.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE BUYER[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Whoever bought the land of the dead towns, demolished what was left and sold it back to the megacorps was almost always [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF][b]Portenova Corp[/b][/color][/url][color=white]. While [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2557482][color=#7FDBFF]Manuella Portenova[/color][/url][color=white] handed out cheap houses in front of the cameras, she decided far from them where Los Vales would live and where it would stop existing.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE SUSPICION[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The most suspicious say some disasters were caused on purpose to push people out — fires, contaminated wells, roads left to collapse. Nothing was ever proven. The Great Fire of [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]La Maria[/color][/url][color=white] in 2039 is the case people cite most, because Portenova bought the ashes.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE EXODUS[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Between 2030 and 2050 about 1,200 towns died and some 41 million people moved. Few of them chose where to go. A town lost its hospital, then its school, then its water, and the families followed the last bus to whichever city was hiring that year. The Monopolization was only the largest of the great movements that made Los Vales.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE GHOST CITIES[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Most dead towns were demolished and sold. A few were not: nobody bought them, or the price of the ruins was higher than the price of the land. Four ghost cities still stand in Los Vales. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Valewood[/color][/url][color=white] rents them as film sets; [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832716][color=#7FDBFF]the Thirsty[/color][/url][color=white] Ones and the Unregistered live in them; [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999868][color=#7FDBFF]Lockwell[/color][/url][color=white] uses one as a camp.[/color]

[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]THE FAVELA[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]The [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2830623][color=#7FDBFF]Illuminated Favela[/color][/url][color=white] is older than the city it lights. [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Zyxtopia[/color][/url][color=white] opened as the capital in 2046, but its walls began to rise in 2038, on the site of an old [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999863][color=#7FDBFF]Nakama State[/color][/url][color=white] town. Eight years of building needed hundreds of thousands of hands, and the workers lived where they could: in a camp outside the wall they were building. By 2046 about 400,000 people lived there. Nobody sent them away when the work was done.[/color]

[color=white]The camp kept growing. The last families of the dead towns of the Nakama State had nowhere else to go, and by 2049 about 1.3 million people lived against the wall — which is why the Union’s Operation Favela Line could kill 540,000 of them that June. The [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2834884][color=#7FDBFF]Rebirth Plan[/color][/url][color=white] rebuilt Valewood and [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=1999863][color=#7FDBFF]Route 69[/color][/url][color=white]. It rebuilt nothing in the Favela, and the Favela rebuilt itself. Nobody counts it now; [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832716][color=#7FDBFF]the Beacons[/color][/url][color=white], who sell it its light, think it holds about four million people.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[table=plain][tr][td]
[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]SEVEN CITIES[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]What remains are the seven metropolises — [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Ferox[/color][/url][color=white], [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832735][color=#7FDBFF]Universalia[/color][/url][color=white], La Maria, Zyxtopia, [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Las Dulces[/color][/url][color=white], [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2530927][color=#7FDBFF]Las Noites[/color][/url][color=white] and Valewood — each one, in practice, the property of the corporations. Those who did not fit went to the [/color][color=white][b]Illuminated Favela[/b][/color][color=white] outside Zyxtopia’s walls, or to the abandoned villages of the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2830623][color=#7FDBFF]Escaldar[/color][/url][color=white], where the Thirsty Ones still bring water.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]

[size=130][color=#8FE3FF][b]A COUNTRY THAT NEVER DECLARES WAR[/b][/color][/size]

[color=white]Los Vales has never declared a war abroad. Its corporations have fought in almost all of them. The rule, written down for the first time after the [/color][url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=dispatch/id=2832728][color=#7FDBFF]Strait War[/color][/url][color=white], is simple: the State stays neutral, and everything else is for sale.[/color]
[/td][/tr][/table]
